# Sorted slices

Binary search and bounds over a slice that is already in order, and checking that it is.

<h2 id="is-sorted"><code>IsSorted&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsSorted<T>(items: T[..]) -> bool
```

Whether `items` is in non-decreasing order.
`items` is borrowed and read. An empty slice and a single element are sorted, there being no pair to be out of
order. Equal neighbours are in order: this asks for non-decreasing, not strictly increasing.
Requires `<` on the element type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length, stopping at the first pair out of order, and allocates
nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L27)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |

**Returns**: whether the sequence is in non-descending order

<h2 id="is-sorted-until"><code>IsSortedUntil&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsSortedUntil<T>(items: T[..]) -> uint
```

How far `items` is in non-decreasing order.
`items` is borrowed and read. Returns the length of the longest sorted run starting at the front, which is the
whole length when the slice is sorted, and the index of the first element smaller than the one before it
otherwise. An empty slice gives zero and a single element gives one.
Requires `<` on the element type.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the answer and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L41)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |

**Returns**: how many leading elements are in non-descending order

<h2 id="lower-bound"><code>LowerBound&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func LowerBound<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint
```

The first position where `value` could be inserted without breaking the order.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. This is the index of the first element not less than
`value` — the first equal one when there are equals, and where it would go when there are none. A value larger
than everything gives the length.
Requires `<` on the element type, and requires `items` to be sorted by that order.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L62)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to place      |

**Returns**: the first index where `value` could be inserted and keep the order

<h2 id="upper-bound"><code>UpperBound&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UpperBound<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint
```

The last position where `value` could be inserted without breaking the order.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. This is the index of the first element greater than
`value` — one past the last equal one when there are equals, and the same as [`LowerBound`](/docs/api/algorithms/sorted-slices#lower-bound) when there are none.
Requires `<` on the element type, and requires `items` to be sorted by that order.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L87)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to place      |

**Returns**: the last index where `value` could be inserted and keep the order

<h2 id="binary-search"><code>BinarySearch&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func BinarySearch<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint?
```

The index of an element of `items` equal to `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. Reports `none` when no element is equal. When several
are, the one reported is the first of them, which makes the answer depend on the sequence rather than on how the
search happened to divide it.
Requires `<` on the element type, and requires `items` to be sorted by that order. Equality is decided by the
ordering rather than by `==`: two elements neither of which is less than the other are equal here, whatever `==`
would say about them.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L115)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to look for   |

**Returns**: the index of a matching element, or `none`; which one is unspecified when several match

<h2 id="equal-range"><code>EqualRange&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func EqualRange<T>(items: T[..], value: T) -> uint..uint
```

The range of positions in `items` holding elements equal to `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. The range runs from [`LowerBound`](/docs/api/algorithms/sorted-slices#lower-bound) to [`UpperBound`](/docs/api/algorithms/sorted-slices#upper-bound), so it
is empty when no element is equal — and its `start` is then where the value would be inserted, which is the
answer a caller inserting into a sorted sequence wants.
Requires `<` on the element type, and requires `items` to be sorted by that order.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L132)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name    | Type    | Description             |
| ------- | ------- | ----------------------- |
| `items` | `T[..]` | the sequence to work on |
| `value` | `T`     | the value to bracket    |

**Returns**: the range of indices holding elements equal to `value`, empty when none does

<h2 id="is-sorted-by"><code>IsSortedBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsSortedBy<T>(
    items: T[..],
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> bool
```

Whether `items` is in non-decreasing order under `compare`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `compare` is called once per neighbouring pair until one is out of order. An empty
slice and a single element are sorted, and equal neighbours are in order.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever `compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L145)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`                  | the sequence to work on                   |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: whether the sequence is in non-descending order under `compare`

<h2 id="is-sorted-until-by"><code>IsSortedUntilBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func IsSortedUntilBy<T>(
    items: T[..],
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> uint
```

How far `items` is in non-decreasing order under `compare`.
`items` is borrowed and read. Returns the length of the longest sorted run starting at the front, exactly as
[`IsSortedUntil`](/docs/api/algorithms/sorted-slices#is-sorted-until) does for the element type's own order.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the answer and allocates nothing beyond whatever `compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L158)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`                  | the sequence to work on                   |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: how many leading elements are in non-descending order under `compare`

<h2 id="lower-bound-by"><code>LowerBoundBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func LowerBoundBy<T>(
    items: T[..],
    value: T,
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> uint
```

The first position where `value` could be inserted into `items` under `compare` without breaking the order.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. `compare` must be the order `items` was sorted by.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever
`compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L178)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`                  | the sequence to work on                   |
| `value`   | `T`                      | the value to place                        |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: the first index where `value` could be inserted and keep the order under `compare`

<h2 id="upper-bound-by"><code>UpperBoundBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func UpperBoundBy<T>(
```

<h2 id="binary-search-by"><code>BinarySearchBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func BinarySearchBy<T>(
    items: T[..],
    value: T,
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> uint?
```

The index of an element of `items` that `compare` calls equal to `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. Reports `none` when no element is equal, and the first of
them when several are. `compare` must be the order `items` was sorted by.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever
`compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L229)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`                  | the sequence to work on                   |
| `value`   | `T`                      | the value to look for                     |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: the index of a matching element under `compare`, or `none`

<h2 id="equal-range-by"><code>EqualRangeBy&lt;T&gt;</code></h2>

```rux
pub func EqualRangeBy<T>(
    items: T[..],
    value: T,
    compare: func(T, T) -> Ordering
) -> uint..uint
```

The range of positions in `items` holding elements `compare` calls equal to `value`.
`items` is borrowed and read; `value` is read by value. Empty when no element is equal, with its `start` at the
position the value would be inserted. `compare` must be the order `items` was sorted by.
Cannot fail. Runs in time proportional to the logarithm of the length and allocates nothing beyond whatever
`compare` does.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Algorithms/Src/Search.rux#L246)

**Type parameters**

| Name | Description      |
| ---- | ---------------- |
| `T`  | the element type |

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                     | Description                               |
| --------- | ------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- |
| `items`   | `T[..]`                  | the sequence to work on                   |
| `value`   | `T`                      | the value to bracket                      |
| `compare` | `func(T, T) -> Ordering` | how two elements order against each other |

**Returns**: the range of indices holding elements equal to `value` under `compare`
